text_content: 6 1. Login to e-GP Portal along with Email Id & Password Procuring Entity (PE) will be created by e-GP Admin/Organization Admin/PE Admin in the e-GP Portal. The moment PE is created on e-GP Portal; PE will get a system generated e-mail in his registered e-mail address which contains the necessary information pertaining to PE login details along with Username & Password. With the help of this Username & Password, PE can start working on e-GP Portal. (As shown in Screen –A1). Steps for Login to the system 1.1 When accessing the e-GP Portal, PE (Procuring Entity) User will initiate the login process by providing their designated User Name and Password. 1.2 For users logging in for the first time, a security and integrity measure is implemented. In this scenario, the e-GP system will guide the PE to a "Change Password" screen. This is a crucial step aimed at enhancing the overall security of the e-GP Portal. 1.3 On the "Change Password" screen, the PE will be prompted to provide specific details as requested. This process ensures that the PE's account remains secure and aligned with the portal's integrity standards. Screen–A1 1.4 It is important to note that within the "Change Password" page, all fields are designated as mandatory. This means that the Procuring Entity (PE) User must provide input for every single field on this page.

detected_section: General / Introduction
text_content: 7 1.5 After the Procuring Entity (PE) User has provided all the necessary inputs on the "Change Password" page, he has to click on the "Submit" button to proceed. As shown in Screen-A2. Screen-A2 1.6 After the Procuring Entity (PE) User has provided the required details and clicked on the "Submit" button, the system will display a confirmation message “Password Changed successfully”. This message signifies that the password change process was completed without any issues. (As shown in Screen-A3). Screen-A3 1.7 After the successful password change process, the Procuring Entity (PE) User is required to proceed with logging in. To do this, the PE should enter their registered email ID (associated with their e-GP Portal account) and the newly set password in the respective fields within the login box. 1.8 Once the PE has entered their email ID and updated password, he can proceed by clicking on the "Login" button. This action will authenticate his credentials and grant access to the e-GP Portal with the newly set password, allowing to continue activities within the system.

detected_section: General / Introduction
text_content: 8 1.9 Upon successfully logging into the system, there are two possible scenarios depending on the verification status of the email address and mobile number associated with the user account: • Verified Email and Mobile Number: If both the email address and mobile number have been previously verified, the system will automatically redirect the user to the e-GP dashboard. • Unverified Email or Mobile Number: In the event that either the email address or mobile number is not verified, a specific page will be displayed to the user. This page, as shown in Screen-A4, is designed to facilitate the verification of the user's National ID and Mobile Number. Completing this verification process is essential to ensure the security and authenticity of the user's account before granting access to the e-GP dashboard. Screen-A4 1.10 The process of verifying your National ID and Mobile Number is optional, and you have the choice to skip this step by clicking on the "Update Later" button. However, it's important to note that if you choose to skip verification, the system will continue to display the verification screen every time you log in. 1.11 To verify your National ID, follow these steps: • Enter National ID Number: Input your National ID Number into the designated field. • Date of Birth: Provide your Date of Birth as per the required format. • Captcha Verification: In the text box displayed, accurately reproduce the characters shown in the captcha image. If needed, you can refresh the captcha text by clicking on the reload icon located beside the captcha image.

detected_section: General / Introduction
text_content: 9 • Verify NID: After ensuring all the information is correctly entered, click on the "Verify NID" button. This action will initiate the verification process for your National ID. (As shown in Screen-A4). 1.12 After clicking on “Verify Button”, a warning message will appear in a pop-up window. This message will inform you of the remaining number of attempts you have to successfully verify your National ID. Each user is granted a total of three attempts to verify their National ID. If, unfortunately, you fail to successfully verify your National ID within the allotted three attempts, the system will automatically lock the verification process. At this point, you may need to contact the system administrator to unlock the process and attempt verification again. As shown in Screen-A5. 1.13 Click on "Yes" to continue, please select this option if you wish to proceed with the action presented. (As shown in Screen-A5). Screen-A5 1.14 After clicking the "Yes" button, the system will initiate a process to verify the data you provided with the National ID (NID) server. 1.15 Upon the successful verification of your National ID, the system will retrieve your name and name in Bangla from the server. A success message will appear in a pop-up window, stating "NID Verification Successful." This message confirms that your National ID verification was completed successfully, and your provided information matches the records on the server. As shown in Screen-A6.

detected_section: General / Introduction
text_content: 10 Screen-A6 1.16 Upon successful verification of your National ID through the National ID server, the system will display a status indicator “ NID Verified” next to the National ID field. (As shown in Screen-A7). Screen-A7 1.17 To complete the National ID Verification process, click on the "Update NID Information" button. (As shown in Screen-A8). Screen-A8

detected_section: General / Introduction
text_content: 11 1.18 After successfully verifying your National ID, during subsequent logins to the system, you will not encounter the National ID verification screen again. However, if your mobile number is still pending verification, you may encounter a mobile number verification block during subsequent logins. (As shown in Screen-A9). 1.19 To verify your mobile phone number, follow these steps: • Enter your mobile phone number into the designated field. • After entering your mobile number, click on the "Send OTP" button. • The system will then send a one-time password (OTP) to the provided mobile number. This OTP is a unique code that you will need to complete the verification process. (As shown in Screen-A9). Screen-A9 1.20 Enter the OTP into the designated field on the verification screen. Ensure that you enter the OTP before it expires; OTPs typically have a limited validity period. After entering the OTP, click on the "Verify OTP" button. (As shown in Screen-A10). Screen-A10

detected_section: General / Introduction
text_content: 12 1.21 Upon successfully verifying the OTP (one-time password), the system will display a status indicator “ OTP Verified”. (As shown in Screen-A11). Screen-A11 1.22 Typically, the validity of an OTP (one-time password) is set to 5 minutes from the time it is sent. If, for any reason, the OTP expires before you can successfully use it for verification then click on the "Try Again" link. The system will then resend a fresh OTP to your registered mobile number. (As shown in Screen-A12). Screen-A12 1.23 After successfully verifying your mobile number with the OTP, click on “Update Mobile Number” button. 1.24 Once your mobile number is updated and verified, the system will no longer display the mobile number verification block when you log in to the e-GP system.

As shown in Screen – G59 Screen – G59 6.1.77 TEC find the exceptions in the process for the following scenarios: 6.1.77.1 For ICT tender, Evaluated Amount will be calculated as follows: ▪ Currency wise evaluated amount will be converted to equivalent BDT. ▪ “Custom Duties, import VAT & other import taxes” deducted from BDT amount. 6.1.77.2 For ICB (Procurement Type) Works Tender, Provisional Sum is not added in the Price Comparison Report (PCR). 6.1.77.3 For Limited Tendering Method (LTM), lottery will be appeared here then “Lottery” options will be available in the Price Comparison Report. Note: ▪ After the lottery, information of winning bidders such as Tenderer Registration Details, Company Details and Personal Details link will be available in the Tender Evaluation Committee dashboard. ▪ In case of LTM tender, if the winner is disqualified and the lottery happens three times simultaneously then “Send To HOPE” button will be available in the system for re-tendering.

text_content: 250 6.1.78 Once the “Price Comparative Report” or “Lottery” gets saved then system will generate the Wining Tenderer/Consultant, TER3 and TER4. (As shown in Screen – G60). Screen – G60 6.1.79 Significantly Low-Priced Tenders will not be applicable for a single responsive tender. (As shown in Screen – G61). In such case, the quoted price will have to be compared with the official estimated cost. If the difference between the quoted price of the single tender and the official estimated cost is more than “-” 20%, then that tender will not be accepted and the “Send to HOPE” button will be generated. If the difference between the quoted price of the single tender and the official estimated cost is “-” 20% or less, then after clicking “Save Report” this Tenderer will show as winner. (As shown in Screen – G62). Screen – G61

text_content: 510 Document last selling Date: The document selling period is the timeframe during which interested tenderer can purchase the tender documents. Tender Closing Date and Time: The tender closing date and time represent the deadline for the submission of proposals or bids. Tender Opening Date and Time: The tender opening date is when the submitted tenders are opened. Selling Tender Document (Principal): The document selling place (who published the Tender). Opening Tender Document: The tender opening place. Receiving Tender Document: The tender Receiving place. Selling Tender Document (Others): Other places of tender document selling. Place of Pre-Tender Meeting: Pre-Tender meeting places. Pre - Tender meeting Date and Time: Pre-Tender meeting may be scheduled to provide interested tenderer with an opportunity to ask questions, seek clarifications, or receive additional information related to the tender and must conclude before the tender closing time.
